title: events_*.json — authored civic events, the unit a story is assembled from
$comment: Shape validation only. FOUR further checks run in CivicEventCatalogLoader and cannot be expressed here: every effect id must exist in the closed effect palette (effects.perEffect); every metricId on a metric/delta spec must exist in MetricRegistry at the declared scope; the five census-gated metric ids may carry a delta spec but never an absolute one; and every unlock id must appear in this document family's featureIds allow-list. The last two exist because an Absent spec NEGATES whatever it resolves to, so an id resolving to nothing fires Met on every city forever, silently.

featureIds.$comment: The allow-list of progression feature ids an unlock spec in ANY events_*.json may name. Feature ids are raw PrefabSystem.GetPrefabName strings (wave 1 ruling 4) — nothing can check them against the game from here, so declaring them is the only thing standing between a typo and a trigger that reads as never-unlocked forever. The lists union across documents: an unlock in events_eu.json may name an id declared in events_global.json. Confirming these against a real save is wave 1's unwalked manual gate 11.

severity.$comment: The existing 1-5 integer, NOT a new enum. StoryTiers projects it onto Mandatory/Major/Minor through stories.mandatorySeverityThreshold and stories.majorSeverityThreshold. Be conservative: mandatory should feel rare, and AffinityEngine.EventTerm's severity/5 scaling is only honest if the range is used.

relativeToBaseline.$comment: True measures against StorySlot.BaselineMetric — the reading captured when the story opened — rather than against an absolute number. This is what makes the two-month cycle mean something: drafting at M and resolving at M+1 is a genuinely later measurement.

districtAffinity.$comment: District archetypes that feel this hardest. Empty means evenly.

notes.$comment: Authoring note, never rendered and never a prompt input. Required by content review to state the EXPECTED TRIGGER FREQUENCY — 'a mid-size city should see this perhaps twice a decade'. The design document says twice that every threshold must be hittable in a normal game, and this is where the author records the reasoning that claim rests on.

spec.$comment: Declarative, never code per event. A kind that cannot be expressed here is a reason to widen TriggerKind in a reviewed commit, not to special-case one catalog entry.

kind.$comment: "policy" is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from this enum. No sensor writes CitySnapshot.ActivePolicyIds — it is plumbed through SensorMerge and SnapshotAssembly and populated by nothing — so a policy spec can never fire, and an absent policy spec fires on every city forever. The loader rejects it by name with that reason; the schema refuses it one step earlier. "manual" never fires from the city and is never pooled, so an authored event carrying one can never produce a story.

metricId.$comment: For metric/delta: a name from MetricRegistry, checked at the declared scope. For unlock: a progression feature id, which must appear in featureIds. For absent: whichever of the two it resolves to. Empty for manual.

threshold.$comment: Required by the loader for every kind that compares a number. Not defaulted: 0.0 is a real threshold rather than an obviously-absent one, so a missing threshold is an error rather than a silent zero.

windowMonths.$comment: Delta only. The loader additionally bounds this above by scheduler.snapshotRetention - 1, read from tuning: a window wider than the retained history can never be answered and would evaluate Unmeasurable for the life of every save. No delta may name unlockedFeatureIds or industryTaxRates — both are lists, and MetricHistory stores one double per series per month, so no historical series stands behind either.

effectList.$comment: Effect IDS only — no magnitude and no duration. Story effects are scaled by stories.activeEffectScale / successEffectScale / failureEffectScale and clamped against the palette's own declared caps, so an authored magnitude here would be a second, unclamped copy of a number the palette already owns. An event's prose may only claim what these ids can actually do: see the mapping table in docs/plans/0004-event-system-rework.md, which records what is reachable and what is not.

issuePressure.$comment: Per-issue voter pressure. This is the mechanism the whole rework exists for: a positive outcome moves voters toward the government and a negative one away. An unstated issue is simply not pressed. Keys are the Issues.ToKey vocabulary; an unknown key is warned and ignored.
